trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.

Going up would leave number 2 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going left would leave number 2 unreachable without crossing a higher number (and 1 more option fails too). So the line goes right.
Going right, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes down.
Going left would leave number 3 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes down.
The line must go right: around the edge to (1,3) is number 7, which comes later; left is number 6, which comes later.
Number 3 is only reachable this way.
Going around the edge to (5,1) would leave number 4 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes up.
Number 4 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going left would wall in number 11, the last number; going up would leave number 5 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes around the edge to (3,1).
Number 5 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Cell (4,2) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Cell (5,1) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes around the edge to (1,1).
Going down would force the line onto number 9 before its turn. So the line goes right.
The line must go right: down is number 10, which comes later.
Going down would leave both number 10 and cell (3,4) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Going left would leave both number 10 and cell (3,4) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes around the edge to (2,1).
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
